decisions.reason: The integral-only F7 did not specify birationality for reducible curves. Added the generic-point bijection and generic-stalk convention in Given, matching Stacks 01RO; verified finite component restrictions, the product integral-closure computation, and the common-field comparison. The claim and AC assumption are unchanged.

F7 incorrectly attributed coherence to the Euler-characteristic definition. Separated that assertion into F9 with the actual coherent-module definition and the proper/finite-type Noetherian suppliers. Checked exact invertible tensor preserves injectives, the natural degree-zero projection map, resolution comparison, and the k-linear acyclic-image comparison; no extra assumptions on f are needed.

The complete Definition of def-rees-algebra-ideal-sheaf ends by explicitly defining the Rees algebra and its relative Proj for any quasi-coherent ideal; thus F2 is licensed despite its opening finite-type specialization. The locality lemma also explicitly extends blowup notation in Remarks. Restriction commutes with ideal powers and direct sums, and the supplied relative-Proj theorem allows arbitrary quasi-coherent graded algebras, so all four steps are valid.

F4 was false for degree d>1: f/u has degree d-1, whereas the chart ideal is generated by f/u^d. Corrected the dehomogenization formula; its actual use has d=1, so the incidence proof remains valid. Made the zero-degree base case in the kernel induction explicit and cited the actual exceptional-subscheme definition. Checked the kernel induction over arbitrary B, both chart rings, reciprocal-ratio overlap, and P1_B exceptional gluing, including B=0.

The spectrum definition is expressly topological and does not supply F4 as a scheme identification. Replaced it with the published principal-localization open-immersion lemma, whose Statement gives exactly that identification. Chart embeddings in A_a prove reducedness/domains; restricting each chart to its D(fi) gives the common off-center open, dense in every nonempty domain chart, proving global irreducibility. Zero ideals give empty reduced blowups and are excluded only from integrality. Also explicitly derived affine-local and subring reducedness from the reduction definition, instead of attributing them as supplied assertions.

The cited closure lemma requires a Noetherian ambient scheme and did not establish the claimed kernel identification in the stated generality. Replaced that use with a complete chart argument: ker(C -> (C/H)_a)=(H:a^infinity), exact localization identifies the kernel sheaf on every principal refinement, the intrinsic kernels glue, and reverse inclusion of ideals proves minimality. The strict transform therefore exists without a Noetherian assumption; its saturation, reducedness and iteration interfaces are preserved. No new prerequisite is necessary.

F3 incorrectly attributed the exceptional ideal to the construction definition, which explicitly postpones E. Restated F3 as the relative-Proj construction and used F2 alone for admissibility; F2 clause 3 actually identifies E with V(I O_Bl) as an effective Cartier divisor. The two universal properties give maps in both directions, and uniqueness of admissible endomorphisms makes both composites identities. The claim is unchanged.

Step 2.1 falsely identified the entire ratio chart overlap with D(fi fj); for I=(x,y), Spec k[x,T,T^-1] contains x=0 points. Replaced it with gluing on the whole inverse image of each base overlap, where the structural map is an isomorphism by step 1.1. This also covers overlaps of different affine base neighborhoods. Corrected F3 to attribute the chart cover to F1 and removed an ill-typed inverse-image description in step 4.1. Verified chart containment over D(fi), both inverse identities, the universal-property characterization and the set-theoretic exceptional complement.

downstream_reviews.affected_use:
For a reduced curve $D$ on a regular surface, blowing up a closed point with
two-dimensional regular local ring gives the formula
$$\pi^*D=D'+mE,$$
where $m$ is the order of its local equation at that point. This formula is
proved in [[lem-total-transform-strict-plus-exceptional-multiplicity]]; it is
not part of the definition for arbitrary centers. For example, on
$\mathbb A^2_k$, the blowup of $(x^2)$ is the identity, its exceptional Cartier
divisor is $2V(x)$, and the strict transform of $V(x)$ is empty. No integer
$m$ expresses $V(x)$ as $m\cdot2V(x)$.
downstream_reviews.reason: The (x^2) example still has identity blowup and empty strict transform of V(x), because saturation by x^2 is the unit ideal.

downstream_reviews.affected_use:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Euler-characteristic and
blowup suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field,
$X=\mathbb P^2_k$, let $p\in X(k)$ be a $k$-rational point, let
$\pi:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup
([[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]]), let $E=\pi^{-1}(p)$ be the exceptional
curve ([[def-exceptional-divisor-blowup]]) and let
$l:=\pi^*\mathcal O_X(1)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ (the pullback of the
hyperplane class; it is also the strict transform of any line not passing
through $p$). Then
$$l\cdot l=1,\qquad l\cdot E=0,\qquad E\cdot E=-1,$$
so the intersection form on the sublattice $\mathbb Zl+\mathbb ZE$ of
$\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Moreover the strict transform $m:=\pi^*\mathcal O(1)-E$ of a line through $p$
([[def-strict-transform-closed-subscheme]]) satisfies $m=l-E$, $m\cdot E=1$
and $m\cdot m=0$.
downstream_reviews.reason: The line strict transforms still mean the same saturated subschemes, so their divisor classes l and l-E are unchanged.

downstream_reviews.affected_use:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf
of finite type on a scheme $X$
([[def-quasi-coherent-ideal-sheaf]]), let
$\pi\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\to X$ be the blowup of
[[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]] with center $Z=V(\mathcal I)$, and let
$W\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme
([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]). Write
$\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ for the inverse image ideal of
$\mathcal I$ in $W$; it is a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of finite type, and
it cuts out the scheme-theoretic intersection $W\cap Z$. Then the strict
transform $W'$ of $W$ ([[def-strict-transform-closed-subscheme]]), the
scheme-theoretic closure of $\pi^{-1}(W\smallsetminus Z)$ in
$W\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$, is canonically isomorphic over
$W$ to the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}W$; equivalently, $W'$ is
the blowup of $W$ along the closed subscheme $W\cap Z$. On the standard
affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with
$\mathcal I=(f_0,\dots,f_r)$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$, the chart
$\operatorname{Spec}A[\mathcal I/f_i]$ of the blowup meets $W'$ in
$\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(A[\mathcal I/f_i]\big/\bigl(KA[\mathcal I/f_i]:f_i^\infty\bigr)\Bigr)$:
$W'$ is cut out by the saturation of the pullback ideal of $W$ by the
exceptional equation. Moreover the strict transform of a finite scheme-theoretic
union is the union of the strict transforms; in particular a finite
union of components is transformed componentwise.
downstream_reviews.reason: F1 and the Statement use closure and chart saturation for arbitrary schemes. The repaired unconditional kernel description directly licenses these uses.

Let $C_0\subseteq\mathbb P^2_k$ be a reduced projective plane curve over a field $k$ (equivalently, a reduced hypersurface; reducible $C_0$ is allowed). Let $S$ be the regular projective surface obtained from $\mathbb P^2_k$ by finitely many point blowups at closed points, and let $C\subseteq S$ be the reduced strict transform of $C_0$. Then there is a finite sequence of blowups of closed points of the current regular projective surface after which the following hold: (a) every irreducible component of the resulting strict transform $C^*$ is regular; (b) the total support of $C^*$ together with the exceptional curves is a regular embedded normal-crossing support: all its components are regular, every intersection of two distinct components is transverse (pairwise contact order at most one at each intersection point), and at most two components pass through any point of the regular ambient surface; (c) at a blowup centered at a closed point $p$ of multiplicity $m$ and residue degree $r=[\kappa(p):k]$, the strict transform $C'$ satisfies $\delta_k(C')=\delta_k(C)-r\,m(m-1)/2$, where $\delta_k$ is the normalization defect of the reduced curve ([[def-normalization-defect-of-reduced-curve]]); this identity is the exact statement used for termination, and the multiplicity $m$ is the $\mathfrak m_p$-adic order of a local reduced equation, with $m=0$ when the center misses the current strict transform. This is regular embedded normal-crossing support over the residual residue fields; it does NOT assert that the components are smooth over an imperfect $k$, does not produce a relative SNC divisor with components smooth over $k$, and makes no claim about resolution of singularities in dimension greater than two.
